title: Inspector and hosts: Claude Desktop, Claude Code

concept.heading: A host is configured, not coded; the description is what the host's model reads
paragraphs: MCP Inspector is the debugger: it launches your server, shows the tool list exactly as a host sees it, lets you call a tool with arguments, and prints the JSON-RPC both ways. Use it before every host; when a host misbehaves, Inspector tells you whether the server or the host is wrong.

Claude Desktop reads claude_desktop_config.json; Claude Code reads .mcp.json or a claude mcp add command. Both need a command that works from any directory, which is why the snippet uses uv run --directory <absolute path to middleware> python -m mcp_server.server. A relative path that works in your terminal fails inside a host.

The experiment that matters: connect a host, ask the same question, change one tool description, restart, ask again. Watch which tool the model calls and with what arguments. Write it down in the README; it is the evidence behind the module's explain-it, and the clearest demo you will ever give a client of what a description does.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Adding a connector to a Copilot Studio agent and testing it in the test pane. The config snippet is the connection reference; Inspector is the test pane with the raw request visible.

spec: Replace every TODO in mcp_server/README.md: the Inspector command, a Claude Desktop mcpServers snippet (command uv, args with --directory and mcp_server.server), and a Claude Code .mcp.json snippet. Keep the fenced json blocks valid JSON.
Connect at least one host (Claude Desktop or Claude Code) and ask 'Did Maria Alvarez give this spring?'. Note what was called.

Change the find_donor description to just 'Find a donor', restart the host, ask again, and write at least 200 characters on what changed under the README's last heading. Restore the good description afterwards.
If a host is unavailable on your machine, do the experiment in Inspector with the model-free view (which tool would you pick from this list?) and say so in the write-up.
